t: An imperial duchy created in 1395 for Gian Galeazzo Visconti, who briefly controlled much of northern and central Italy.
Under the Sforza it was one of Renaissance Europe’s richest courts, where Leonardo da Vinci painted the Last Supper.
Fought over in the Italian Wars, it was ruled by Spain from 1535 and Austria from 1706 until Napoleon ended it in 1796–1797.
dyk: Gian Galeazzo Visconti did not inherit his ducal title: he bought it in 1395 from Wenceslas, King of the Romans, for a sum reported as 100,000 florins.
ev: Gian Galeazzo Visconti buys the ducal title from Wenceslas
Gian Galeazzo dies of plague as his armies encircle Florence
Death of Filippo Maria Visconti; the Golden Ambrosian Republic is proclaimed
Francesco Sforza enters Milan as duke
Leonardo da Vinci begins the Last Supper in Santa Maria delle Grazie
Louis XII of France conquers the duchy
Death of Francesco II Sforza; the duchy passes to Charles V
Napoleon enters Milan; the Transpadane Republic replaces the duchy
